correctness.rationale: The ordered-root map to Sym^4(P¹)=P⁴ restricts scheme-theoretically to the pullback of the plane of quartics aT⁴+bT³U+cTU³−aU⁴. Exactness of S₄-invariants over C identifies the quotient with this plane; finiteness, generic degree 24, and flatness follow from the ordered-root map or finite Cohen–Macaulay flatness. An independent exact Sylvester determinant calculation gives all six displayed discriminant coefficients. The linear repeated-root equations have rank two for every projective root: their finite-root cross product is (−2t³,3t⁴+1,−t⁶−3t²), and the homogenization gives [0:0:1] at infinity. Generically the quartic has just one double root, so this degree-six parametrization without base points is its normalization. In the finite chart F'' at the chosen root is 6t(1−t⁴); the roots t=0 and t⁴=1 are triple but not quadruple, and infinity gives the sixth triple-root point by swapping homogeneous coordinates. Their distinct images are nonimmersive and each costs at least one delta. For a≠0 a two-double-root quartic must be the square of T²−pT+q with q²=−1 and p²=−2q, giving four distinct polynomials with nonzero quadratic discriminant. At a=0 with bc≠0 the four roots are simple, and bc=0 gives just the two endpoint triple-root cases. The four two-branch delta contributions and six singular branches use up the arithmetic genus 10, giving precisely nodes and cusps. On each transposition diagonal the residual pair roots give y=2t³(u−v), with y²=t⁸+14t⁴+1; its eight simple zeros give a connected genus-three double cover. The repeated-root projection of the diagonal is finite (unique coefficient point and only finitely many orderings of the residual two roots); no extra isolated components are possible because the diagonal is cut by two equations in a three-dimensional ambient diagonal. Smoothness follows from the fixed-locus theorem, and this identifies the entire projective model. Apart from transpositions a nontrivial permutation forces a triple root, two double roots, or a quadruple root, so fixes no divisor. The generic inertia on each diagonal is exactly its transposition and the reduced ramification statement follows.
residual_risks: Reduced branch and divisorial ramification only. The affine hyperelliptic equation denotes its smooth projective model, and no assertion about scheme structures of stabilizers at special points is needed.
